title: Security services, documentation and Marketplace security products
learningObjective: Describe AWS security features and services (WAF, Firewall Manager, Shield, GuardDuty), where to find AWS security information, third-party security in AWS Marketplace, and Trusted Advisor for identifying issues.
foundation: AWS offers many built-in security services: firewalls for web apps (AWS WAF), DDoS protection (AWS Shield), threat detection (Amazon GuardDuty) and central firewall management (AWS Firewall Manager).
AWS publishes security guidance on the AWS Security Center, the AWS Security Blog and the AWS Knowledge Center.
You can also buy third-party security tools in AWS Marketplace, and AWS Trusted Advisor flags security risks such as open ports or missing MFA.
engineer: AWS WAF: rules (managed rule groups, rate-based rules, IP sets) for CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway and AppSync. AWS Shield Standard: automatic DDoS protection at no extra cost; Shield Advanced: enhanced protection, cost protection and access to the Shield Response Team. AWS Firewall Manager: central policies for WAF, Shield Advanced, security groups, Network Firewall and DNS Firewall across an organisation.
Detect and respond: GuardDuty (threat detection), Inspector, Macie, Security Hub, Detective; network security: security groups, NACLs, AWS Network Firewall.

Security information: AWS Security Center (aws.amazon.com/security), AWS Security Blog, AWS Knowledge Center (on re:Post), security bulletins, whitepapers (for example AWS Security Best Practices), Well-Architected security pillar.
AWS Marketplace: third-party firewalls, antivirus, SIEM and identity products, billed through your AWS account.

Trusted Advisor security checks include S3 bucket permissions, security groups with unrestricted access, IAM use, MFA on root and exposed access keys; the full set of checks depends on the support plan.

animation.caption: Open 'Security services' to match protection needs to services.

example.title: Protecting a public web app
body: A media company fronts its site with CloudFront and AWS WAF managed rules, subscribes to Shield Advanced for DDoS response support, uses Firewall Manager to apply the same WAF rules to every account, and reviews Trusted Advisor security checks weekly.

prerequisites: An AWS account (use an IAM Identity Center user, not root)
permissions: Read-only access to explore; least-privilege permissions to change resources
limits: Conceptual objective: explore in the console; no configuration limits are tested
configuration.cli:
aws wafv2 list-web-acls --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1
aws shield describe-subscription
aws support describe-trusted-advisor-checks --language en

troubleshooting.fix: Add AWS WAF rate-based rules; consider Shield Advanced.

Where to find AWS security information

steps.label: Attack
steps.title: Your shop is attacked on Black Friday
body: One attacker floods the site with traffic. Another sends SQL injection attempts through the login form.
You need protection at the edge, rules for bad requests, and a way to spot trouble inside your account.

steps.label: Shield
steps.title: AWS Shield absorbs DDoS floods
body: AWS Shield Standard is on automatically, free for every customer, and protects against common network-layer DDoS attacks.
Shield Advanced is a paid upgrade. It adds protection against larger attacks, 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS response team, and cost protection for scaling during an attack.

steps.label: WAF
steps.title: AWS WAF filters bad web requests
body: AWS WAF is a web application firewall. Rules block requests that look like SQL injection or cross-site scripting, come from bad IP addresses, or exceed a rate limit.
It protects CloudFront, Application Load Balancers and API Gateway.

callout.text: Shield = DDoS (floods). WAF = malicious web requests (layer 7 rules).

steps.label: Firewall Manager
steps.title: Apply the same rules everywhere
body: You have 30 accounts in AWS Organizations. AWS Firewall Manager sets WAF rules, Shield Advanced protections and security group policies centrally, and applies them to new accounts and resources automatically.

steps.label: Detect
steps.title: Spot threats and risky settings
body: Amazon GuardDuty watches CloudTrail events, VPC flow logs and DNS logs for threats, such as a server talking to a known crypto-mining host.
AWS Trusted Advisor runs best-practice checks, including security ones: open ports, root without MFA, public S3 buckets.

steps.label: Marketplace
steps.title: Need more? Buy it in AWS Marketplace
body: AWS Marketplace sells third-party security products, such as firewalls, endpoint protection and SIEM tools, already packaged to run on AWS, with billing through your AWS bill.

steps.label: Learn more
steps.title: Where to read up on security
body: The AWS Security Center and AWS Security Blog cover best practices and news. The AWS Knowledge Center answers common how-to questions. Security documentation and whitepapers cover each service in depth.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Layers of protection
body: Edge, rules, central policy, detection, and somewhere to learn more.
recap: Firewall Manager: rules across all accounts
GuardDuty: threat detection; Trusted Advisor: best-practice checks
